abstract: Prostate cancer (PCa) is a common malignancy with an increasing incidence in men worldwide. Ferroptosis, an iron-dependent form of programmed cell death mediated by interactions among multiple genes, has emerged as a promising therapeutic target for PCa. Previous work focused on modeling the contribution of literature-reported known ferroptosis-related genes (FRGs) in cancers, in this study a knowledge-guided bioinformatics model was applied by systematically characterizing the topology-function properties in PCa-specific protein-protein interaction network with known FRGs as the prior knowledge to guide the identification of novel ferroptosis-related signatures. The model starts at a random walk with restart algorithm to extract genes with global topological proximity to FRG seeds, and an integrated prioritization strategy, i.e., node centrality scoring, community module mining, and clinical significance evaluation, was proposed to identify ACTC1 as a top-prioritized candidate triggering PCa ferroptosis. The expression of ACTC1 was significantly negatively correlated with PCa pathological malignancy and biochemical recurrence (p < 0.05). Experimental validations using western blotting, intracellular reactive oxygen species, Fe2+ probe FerroOrange, transmission electron microscopy, and molecular pathway detection, etc., demonstrated that ACTC1 was a biomarker and tumor suppressor with the mechanism of inhibiting PCa development via inducing abnormal intracellular Fe2+ accumulation and ferroptosis. In particular, the over-expression of ACTC1 contributed to changes in Fe2+ homeostasis-associated proteins, i.e., upregulating DMT1/NCOA4 (p < 0.001) and downregulating FPN1 (p < 0.01). Moreover, miR-7-5p was a potential upstream regulator of ACTC1, and it mediated the level of intracellular Fe2+ and reactive oxygen species in PCa ferroptosis (p < 0.001). This study proposed an interpretable pipeline for the screening of ferroptosis-related factors, which holds the applicability to biomarker discovery in other disease scenarios.

summary: Network random-walk model on PCa interactome prioritizes ACTC1 (miR-7-5p-regulated) as ferroptosis regulator; wet-lab validation.
title: Knowledge-guided identification of miR-7-5p/ACTC1 as a ferroptosis regulatory axis mediating intracellular ferrous iron accumulation in prostate cancer.
